First, I'll parse the SVG path data:  
- M 82.48,71.72 → move to starting point  
- L 86.86,76.47 → line to  
- L 74.69,38.07 → line to  
- M 74.69,38.07 → move again (new subpath)  
- L 46.36,43.46 → line to  
- L 40.46,60.21 → line to  
- L 76.97,78.68 → line to  
- L 82.48,71.72 → line back to start  

The first subpath has 3 points (including the M), so it's a line segment from (82.48,71.72) to (86.86,76.47) to (74.69,38.07). That's two line segments, not a closed shape.  

The second subpath starts at (74.69,38.07), goes to (46.36,43.46), (40.46,60.21), (76.97,78.68), and back to (82.48,71.72). That's 5 points in this subpath, but the last point connects to the first point of the first subpath? No — the last point (82.48,71.72) is the starting point of the first subpath, so the entire path is connected:  

Sequence of points:  
1. (82.48,71.72)  
2. (86.86,76.47)  
3. (74.69,38.07)  
4. (46.36,43.46)  
5. (40.46,60.21)  
6. (76.97,78.68)  
7. (82.48,71.72)  

That's 7 distinct points, with the last returning to the first, forming a closed polygon.  

A polygon with 7 sides is a heptagon.  

Final answer: (B)
